text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German debt prices were heading back towards base in late trade, recovering losses sustained during the day, the market was very quiet, but suffering still from the uncertainty over how Germany plans to plug its deficit holes after the government was forecd to back down on plans to take a one-off payment from Bundesbank reserves. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.45, unchanged from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts struggled off the day's lows but ended down on the day as worries over a rate rise on Friday started to bite, the newly empowered Bank of England's monetary policy committee starts its two-day meeting on Thursday with the outcome to be announced at 1100 GMT on Friday. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 113-02/32, down 12/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - June bond future settles near day's lows as Bund weakness, concern about likely Socialist policies, lack of follow through buying after two days of short covering all weigh. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 129.14, down 0.26 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held at easier levels but were off the day's low as bunds recovered and moved into positive territory, the market was generally uncertain awaiting developments after Bonn appeared to have backed down in German gold revaluation row and the future of EMU after the French socialist victory. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 129.60, down 0.20 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries stay depressed, but losses pared in late morning, short-covering takes Treasuries off lows seen after data, with activity very light. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-13/32, down 02/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.89 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese government bond (JGB) futures closed firmer after two days of losses, the market now considers the September contract to be the new benchmark because its turnover exceeded that of the June this morning. In after hours trading the September future on LIFFE was trading at 122.84, up 0.43 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The new issues market saw another splurge of dollar deals spread across the maturity spectrum and totalling over a billion dollars, while the pace was slower than Tuesaday, players were still rushing to the market ahead of key U.S. jobs data, due on Friday. General Electric Capital Corp led the way with a $350 million deal with a 13-year maturity -- a particular rarity in the Eurobond market -- which was reoffered at a spread of 33 basis points over the on-the-run 10-year U.S. Treasury note by lead manager Goldman Sachs International.
